audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Irelia six of seven rows while the reasons underneath say otherwise: whys[0] 'neither of you wins level 1', whys[3] 'a coin-flip skirmish window', whys[4] 'he owns the level 6 trade' under a 'Skill' label, whys[6] 'He out-tanks you flat at 2+ items'. The packet levelChart and the already-applied mirror audit both read Skill / Irelia / Irelia / Skill / Cho'Gath / Skill / Skill. diff also said FAV 4/10 against a 52.09% win rate.
audit.why: Rupture outranges her step-up at level 1 with no stun to answer; Feast at 6 is flat true damage that beats her sustain; from first item on his stacking blunts her spike without ever losing to it outright.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 3, 4, 5 and 6 set to the mirror's chart in both layers, ratings re-scored, diff moved to EVEN 6/10 with the matching tone and difficulty lines.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one Cho'Gath cooldown appeared in the full layer, and the tracked 'matchup-defining' cooldown was Rupture — the wrong ability. Rupture is telegraphed and on 6s flat; the ability that actually decides whether Irelia's all-in works is Feral Scream.
audit.why: Feral Scream is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s and silences — a silenced Irelia cannot cast Bladesurge, so she has neither engage nor exit. Feast is 80/70/60s. Rupture's 6s cooldown is too short to plan around, which is exactly why it should not be the tracked ability.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns retargeted onto Feral Scream with its 11s rank-1 number; Feast's 80s written into phases[4].why and dontsFull[2].d.
sources: enemyKit W cd 11/10.5/10/9.5/9 and silence flag

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer stated no interaction at all — every do and don't was generic filler. Three real ones were missing: Feral Scream's silence locking Bladesurge out of the trade, Feast being flat true damage that ignores both Defiant Dance's reduction and Irelia's healing, and Rupture knocking up and grounding. Also, dosFull[1] called Ionian Fervor 'shred'.
audit.why: Riot's text: Feral Scream deals magic damage and Silences; Feast 'deals a high amount of true damage' and grows his maximum health on a kill; Rupture pops enemies into the air, damages and slows, and carries the grounding flag. Ionian Fervor is stacking bonus Attack Speed plus bonus on-hit damage at max stacks — it does not shred resistances.
audit.corrected: Written into dosFull[1], dosFull[2], all three don'ts, breakdown.cooldowns and phases[3..4].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[7] recommended Flash + Ignite on the grounds that the lane is favoured, which no longer holds once diff is EVEN.
audit.why: 52.09% over 430 games is an even lane, not a lane to burn a summoner forcing.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to Flash + Teleport default with Ignite as the aggressive option.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Rupture's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.

edits.before: Vanguard’s Edge walls off his disengage and marks the kill. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Cho'Gath's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Feast (80s at rank 1) is flat true damage — it ignores Defiant Dance and your healing. Never trade under his kill threshold.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Rupture's cooldown.
edits.after: Skill window: full reset uptime lets you dive him, but every Feast stack he banks blunts the spike.

notes: The content layer's 'passive armor-shred' framing appears in spikes[0].text, wants.you[0], late and whys[2] — Ionian Fervor is stacking attack speed plus on-hit damage at max stacks and shreds nothing. I corrected it in the full layer's dosFull[1]; those four content strings still carry it and need a champion-level pass. Following the mirror audit, I ignored the derived 'grounding' flag on Flawless Duet (Riot's text says only damaged, stunned and Marked) and asserted no grounding from Irelia's E.
